production_source_comparison.interpretation: All 285 runtime/build paths match the tested cloud commit. Eight user extensions are retained; post-build documentation and original dynamic-memory/EC research are separately recorded, not counted as part of cloud production verification.

limits: No real hardware setting, PBO effect or stability measurement has been verified.
Only Shimada family 1Ah/model 08h at PCI 1022:153a/BDF 0 is admitted for the new setting API.
The four new limit setters confirm firmware acknowledgement only: verified=false and current_limit=null even when response=1. No automatic retries, rollback, MP1 fallback or OC enable.
Fmax still has acknowledgement only. Rails has only an offline bounded encoding preview; physical targets and its two-command transaction remain unverified.
Original dynamic-memory and EC dynamic-EDC paths remain research-only. Their original Applied/return behavior is not proof of firmware acceptance or effective hardware changes.
Per-core/CCD PM telemetry layout remains unresolved. Other AMD profiles, native PM transport, Intel server controls and board-specific settings remain incomplete.
EL7 means Oracle Linux 7.9 x86_64. Windows/macOS validate the portable core, not a full application port.
QEMU verifies module integration only; Secure Boot and actual register settings were not tested.

visual_review.method: Six original PNGs opened with view_image and visually reviewed
observations: PPT 350 W and temperature 90 C requested values and selected controls are visible in both target renders.
Accepted examples show response 1, Firmware accepted, and Effective limit readback Unavailable / not verified.
Failure examples show response FD and Attempted; not confirmed, with the status that the limit may have changed and no automatic retry.
The new controls, result rows and bottom status fit within the 1200x1100 fixture viewport.
Other pre-existing action buttons may use ellipsized labels; this review does not claim whole-application visual acceptance.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures only; no real firmware setting or readback.
The remaining 1270 desktop PNGs were archived but not individually viewed in this batch.

dynamic_replay.scope:
REA-guided original dynamic-memory and EC-EDC instruction characterization.

The two selected function bodies and the reused PBO constructor execute in
Unicorn. Qt, PCI, EC, timers, the dynamic-EDC refresh callback, and hardware
identity are synthetic boundaries.
No board contract, physical units or real setting success is inferred.
limitations: Full original constructors and actual Qt text parsing are not executed for EDC.
The final EDC refresh callback is stubbed after the original Applied message; it is not a readback proof.
Synthetic discarded EC writes do not establish the real EC API error convention.
No physical board identity, units, safe operating values or EC coordination protocol established.

observations: Six-field UI has a platform-flag-dependent 53..56 vs 56..59 split. The existing constructor-region experiment does not set the second flag for Shimada 153a alone.
Shimada public RSMU 56/57/58/59, argument scaling and capability bit 1 are used for the new one-limit API. It never copies old UI unconditional Applied feedback.
toggle_dynamic_mem: 14 PCI writes, including 50200=1, forced response=1 before command 92, no response read. All 14 injected PCI failure positions continue to return for both input booleans.
dyn_edc apply uses EC bank 1, not SMU: C1 control, C2 selector, C4 policy, C6/C7 and C8/C9, D0..D5. Five input values truncate to 16-bit big-endian pairs.
With the sampled UI selections, nonselected banks receive 65000 (FD E8). Applied is shown before the separately stubbed refresh callback.
get_THM refreshes a PM monitor and reads a stored offset (+3C, or 44 when flag78 is set) as binary32. This is not a verified TctlMax setting readback.
set_to_shimada defines the separate BIOS SMUIO addresses and message table. It does not turn BIOS command IDs or TEST_SMC_MSG helpers into the new RSMU protocol.
REA mixed ABI pseudocode loses parameters on PCI/EC calls. Exact bytes and synthetic instruction traces were used for actual argument values.
Neither the pinned public sources nor these original paths establish the unresolved per-core/CCD PM offsets or dual-rail transaction.
